findings.evidence: Grep hit: line 173 declares `theorem adjoin_prod_root_injective ... (hST : IntermediateField.adjoin K {...} = ...) : S = T`; Mathlib naming conventions say `Function.Injective f` lemmas use the full word `injective`, while `f x = f y ↔ x = y`/equality-reflection lemmas use `_inj`.
findings.fix: Rename it to an `_inj` name such as `adjoin_prod_root_inj`, or restate it as an actual `Function.Injective` theorem on the nonempty-subset indexing function and keep `_injective`.
findings.issue: `adjoin_prod_root_injective` is not stated as `Function.Injective`; it is an equality-reflection implication from equality of generated fields to `S = T`, so the `_injective` suffix advertises the wrong statement shape.

summary: One new theorem uses the wrong injectivity suffix for its statement form.
